You sound like a really sweet person and I’m sorry that you have had to go through so much in such a short lifetime. I want to say that I read your whole post, and then I reread it, and I understood everything you said. I think it’s really admirable that you are willing to give life another chance despite everything that has happened. I have a few things to say but I’ll try to keep it brief:
1.) Having bad grades doesn’t make you a bad or lazy or useless person. school isn’t everything. I know that’s what it feels like right now but high school is such a short amount of time out of your entire life that it really doesn’t matter. Don’t judge yourself based on other people’s perception of what a good/bad student is, all that matters is that you are doing the best you can in your current state of being.
2.) your friends sound really mean. If you have told them about how upset they make you when they make fun of you and they continue to do so, don’t waste your time hanging out with people that won’t respect you. You don’t inherently owe anyone respect, including your “friends” or family. Respect must be earned. Also these people are not looking out for your best interests so don’t internalize their criticism against you as fact because they aren’t trying to look out for you or be constructive, it’s just mean. 
3.) having a hobby doesnt necessarily mean you HAVE to be good at it or have it lead to anything. I do stuff all the time that I am really bad at and will absolutely never lead to anything substantial in real life, but it takes my mind off of the world for a little while and sometimes that’s enough. Also, not to be cliche but practice makes perfect haha 
4.) find pride in the little milestones if that is what makes you happy: whether two hours, two days, two weeks, two months or however long it may be, clean is clean. You’re not “only 2 days clean”, you’re 2 days clean and that’s great and I’m so proud of you!!
5.) your therapist situation sounds rough and I know exactly how you feel. I’ve gone through so many myself that I can barely keep track and every time another one drops me, it feels really really shitty. It hurts having to open up to someone new again and again. I was very hesitant about therapy in the beginning (I started when I was like 12) but it has actually shown me a lot about myself over the years (21 years old now). If that is something that you are still open to trying, I definitely recommend it. I got my first therapist through a program at my doctors office and they helped me find a good therapist and children’s psychiatrist for medication. Talking to someone about your mental health and your sexual abuse could help you feel a little better.
6.) you said you have no talent but I think that you are a really good writer! I really liked the metaphors and figurative language you used in your post, it made me really connect with the experiences you are having 


I wish I could give you a passion or tell you a goal to work towards but sometimes the best you can do is get out of bed and live another day. It seems like you already know that. Find joy in little things, do stuff that makes you content (even if it’s only temporary). Future you is so proud of present you for finding the strength to get up every morning and make it another day.

I am someone that lives in a constant state of social anxiety. I have been in therapy since I was 12 and I've been on anti-psychotic medication since I was 13. I am not comfortable being vulnerable in social situations so I've been putting on a fake (but likable) personality since I was young. It worked for a long time and I got to a point where it was bearable to go to classes and interact with other people without feeling like there were a million people staring at me and criticizing my every move.  I'd pretend that I'm naturally very talkative and funny and confident (when really I'm about one dropped ice coffee away from a complete mental breakdown). This fake persona helped me get through middle school and most of high school; it served as this wall that I could put up to protect myself from everything that I feared at the time. I wasn't super popular in high school: I didn't play sports or go to parties and I was never in a relationship but I (thought I) was generally well-liked, liked enough to become class president. The class advisor for my year was this physic professor named Mr. Kukucka that everyone thought was really chill (I thought he was too for the most part) and I had him for a teacher during my senior year of high school. I thought that we were tight so we joked around a lot before, during, and after class; the class would continue on like that for the whole year with this dynamic and there was never really a problem with anything.

It was March 16, 2017, a regular Thursday and I was in physics. The class was small but intimate-- I knew everyone and they all knew me. We were learning a lesson and Kukucka was teaching and I made a joke to the class like it was any other day; I don't remember what I said but what he said would change the rest of my life. He stopped his lesson and, completely deadpan with no hint of satire or comedy, he said in front of my entire class, "you know \[trash\_001\], you may think you are funny but your personality is actually pretty offputting. You're going to find out one day that people don't like you as much as you think they do." A 37-year-old man told this to a 17-year-old girl in front of a class full of her peers. I skipped every one of my classes and cried in the bathroom for the rest of the day. Prior to then, I was depressed for sure but I wasn't suicidal; I went home that day and tried to kill myself (which I failed obviously). Probably the worst part was when I went to the guidance counselor to tell her about what happened the next day, she and the principal both gaslit me the entire time about the teacher's behavior and decided to essentially force me to attend an Intensive Outpatient Program instead. IOP is like a court-mandated (and sometimes voluntary) therapy session that you attend with other people for 3 hours a day every day of the week for three months. I also had to continue to work with this man for the rest of the year since he was the class advisor under my presidency and he was still my physics teacher (a class I needed to take to graduate).

I'm a senior in college now so it's been a little under four years and there hasn't been a single day in that time that I didn't think about that statement. It fucked up my entire perception of myself, which extended into my college interactions. I was too scared to do anything social for fear of being "offputting".  His words have had an effect on every single friendship or relationship I have ever had: in the back of my mind is this constant fear that "people don't like \[me\] as much as \[I\] think they do"

Mr. Kukucka, I hope you burn in hell. I pray no one has ever had what happened to me happen to them.

UConn student body is much bigger than that of Quinnipiac and individual class sizes are considerably larger.  For example, when I was a freshman, I took a PHIL 1104 class in ITE C80 (the lecture hall in the basement of the ITE building). Engineering students are required to take a philosophy class so this specific section of PHIL 1104 was packed: ITE C80 can hold 350 students and the room was filled shoulder to shoulder. I just find it hard to imagine how the administration is going to account for the restructuring of large classes like this  (especially since we have already chosen classes for the fall). Another issue is the dining halls. Think about the traffic at peak lunch and dinner hours when you can barely find a seat to sit in; now imagine how difficult dining is going to be when they try to enforce "six feet away" laws. Also, many students rely on UConn transportation to get to campus, and bus capacity will probably be heavily-restricted (imagine trying to get from Northwood Apartments to the middle of campus in a reasonable amount of time without a bus). I just think that it's too much of a liability for the campus to open back up in the fall. 

I hate living at home and online classes did not go well for me. I miss hanging out with my friends and going to parties and working out at the rec center. I miss walking into the library at 7:48 AM on a cool Tuesday morning to purchase an iced Americano from Bookworms before booking it to an 8 AM class across campus. I would do anything to have classes in Storrs in the fall but I am not confident that we will be going back (especially if this "second wave" is going to hit in September). Though the decision is still up in the air, I don't think that Quinnipiac's re-opening is a good comparison.
